pr_title: Throttle progress updates from language servers
pr_body:
Fixes #749

Investigating the above-linked issue, it looked like we were getting multiple progress notifications per frame from the language server and notifying project observers for each one.

Since these progress notifications seem to be monotonic/continuous in nature, it doesn't really make sense to update the UI for them faster than the display can refresh. In this PR, I only assign new progress and update if more than 16.6ms has elapsed since the last update. This seems to fix the responsiveness issues I was seeing in #749 while retaining the progress updates.

@as-cii I worry that there may be a lack of understanding causing me to subtly break something about progress here. Can you check my work carefully on this and make sure this makes sense? Thanks!
pr_comments:
Is it just the notify that causes the problem? Could we just only notify after that interval while still setting the pending_work entry?

I think the solution in this PR may be a bit of a bummer because you could get in a state where it looks like the app is waiting on a task which finished quickly when really its waiting on the task after which got ignored.

An alternative solution is some sort of debounce where we delay the notification by 16.6 milliseconds rather than eating them, but that seems more complicated to achieve

> you could get in a state where it looks like the app is waiting on a task which finished quickly when really its waiting on the task after which got ignored

It looks like this doesn't throttle the work *done* notifications (only the "progress" notifications), so I don't think it will affect tasks that finish quickly.

I had noticed this same issue when I worked on #587: initially I had similar thoughts about potentially throttling it to keep up with the refresh rate, but I simply ended up introducing a `yield_now` to give the UI thread a chance to perform a re-render. I believe that regressed in #702, where that `yield_now` was [accidentally removed](https://github.com/zed-industries/zed/pull/702/files#diff-02d1f1a85a2897bb6726ba0eda0245dd944c4bd57cc3911cedc628816efc0fc9L1409-L1410).

Note that I added a similar `yield_now` in the [RPC system](https://github.com/zed-industries/zed/blob/ae415ee49b02dd853cb0b30753cea22d50633fb9/crates/client/src/client.rs#L722-L723) (only for clients) for the same exact reason, the network could send us arbitrarily many messages causing whichever thread is consuming them to starve.

One idea for fixing this is to introduce a `yield_now` at the LSP level after every message we process to prevent the issue described in this pull request. I think that would allow us to avoid making assumptions about the refresh rate of the monitor while giving the main event loop chances to make progress.

issue_context.title: App briefly becomes unresponsive upon starting a language server for the first time
issue_context.body:
- Open Zed in release mode
- Open a large Rust file so the language server starts
- Hold the down arrow to move the cursor down
- Observe that we skip frames

review_comments:
Do you think it's worth avoiding the network traffic required to to broadcast these ignored progress updates from the host to guests?

One way to do that would be to return a boolean from this method, where `false` would indicate that this update should be suppressed. The caller of this code, `Project::on_lsp_progress`, could avoid broadcasting the update in that case.
